# A uniform lower bound for the saturated-positive limiting cap

For independent X~Gamma(k,1) and E~Exp(1), put

    G_k=Pr(X>=E+k-1),       k>=1.

Then

    G_k>9/20                                               (1)

for every integer k>=1. Combined with
`candidate a6e6fd61fe60c16a`,
this bounds every capped balanced exponential sum whose positive
coefficients are all one and whose negatives include a fixed one.
It does not treat a fractional positive coefficient or general OC.

The proof is analytic for every k>=76 and uses the finite integer
certificate below for k<=75. No probabilistic approximation or numerical
floating-point estimate enters either part.

## 1. Elementary factorial and Poisson bounds

Let m>=1, p_m=e^(-m)m^m/m!, and

    A_m=e^(-m)sum_(j=0)^m m^j/j!.

Then A_m>1/2. Indeed A_m is the survival probability at m of a
Gamma(m+1,1) variable, whose density g(x)=x^m e^(-x)/m! satisfies,
for 0<s<m,

    log(g(m+s)/g(m-s))
      =m log((1+s/m)/(1-s/m))-2s>0.

The last inequality follows by integrating the derivative
2/(1-u^2)>2 from zero to s/m. Integrating the density comparison over
(0,m), then adding the positive tail beyond 2m, proves A_m>1/2.

Concavity of log on each interval [j-1/2,j+1/2] gives

    log(m!)>=integral_(1/2)^(m+1/2) log x dx
      =(m+1/2)log(m+1/2)-m+(1/2)log 2.

Since log(1+x)>=x/(1+x) for x>=0, this implies

    log(m!)>=(m+1/2)log m-m+(1/2)log(2e).

Thus p_m<=1/sqrt(2em). The elementary series lower bound
e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3 yields

    p_m<sqrt(3/(16m)).                                     (2)

## 2. The unbounded range

The exact gamma-tail identity with m=k-1>=1 is

    G_(m+1)=e^(-m)sum_(j=0)^m (m^j/j!)(1-2^(-(m+1-j))).

Write the second term as B_m. Reindex j=m-l to get

    B_m=p_m sum_(l=0)^m 2^(-(l+1))
                   [m(m-1)...(m-l+1)/m^l] <p_m.

Every bracket is at most one, and the finite geometric sum is less than
one. Hence G_(m+1)=A_m-B_m>1/2-p_m. For m>=75, (2) gives
p_m<1/20, and (1) follows. This proves the bound uniformly over the
entire infinite range, with an explicit endpoint.

## 3. A finite rational certificate for the remaining integers

The exponential series gives e<87/32. More explicitly, its sum through
degree five is 163/60, and its tail from degree six is at most
(1/720)sum_(r>=0)7^(-r)=7/4320. The sum of these two bounds is
87/32-1/2160, so the strict bound follows.

Define the positive integer

    Z_m=sum_(j=0)^m (2^(m+1)-2^j)(m!/j!)m^j.

For m>=1 the exact tail formula and e<87/32 give

    G_(m+1)> Z_m 32^m/[2^(m+1)m!87^m].                       (3)

Here is an integer certificate for m=1,...,74. In the displayed order,
the integers r_m below satisfy

    100000 Z_m 32^m >= r_m 2^(m+1)m!87^m.                    (4)

    45977,45659,45718,45852,45999,46140,46270,46389,46497,46595,
    46684,46766,46841,46909,46973,47031,47085,47135,47182,47225,
    47266,47304,47339,47373,47404,47433,47461,47487,47512,47535,
    47557,47577,47597,47616,47633,47650,47665,47680,47694,47708,
    47720,47732,47744,47755,47765,47774,47784,47792,47800,47808,
    47815,47822,47829,47835,47841,47846,47851,47856,47861,47865,
    47869,47872,47876,47879,47882,47884,47887,47889,47891,47893,
    47894,47896,47897,47898.

Each is greater than 45000. These small finite arithmetic inequalities
may be checked directly from the definition of Z_m; an equivalent
division-free-in-value recurrence starts at c_m=m^m and uses
c_(j-1)=j c_j/m, where every division is exact, to obtain
c_j=(m!/j!)m^j. Sum (2^(m+1)-2^j)c_j to obtain Z_m.
The accompanying verifier checks both integer constructions independently
and checks (4) by cross multiplication, without approximating e or any
probability. Equations (3)--(4) prove (1) for these remaining integers.
Finally k=1 gives G_1=Pr(Exp(1)>=Exp(1))=1/2. This completes all cases.
